title: Towards Verifying Exact Conditions for Implementations of Density Functional Approximations
problem: Implementations of Density Functional Approximations used extensively in scientific computing lack formal verification that they satisfy known exact mathematical conditions. This creates uncertainty about correctness of critical simulations in materials science and computational chemistry.
motivation: Density Functional Theory is foundational to computational materials science and chemistry, making verification of DFA implementations essential for trustworthy scientific results.
method: XCVerifier applies formal verification methods to check whether DFA implementations satisfy analytically-derived exact conditions. The tool was evaluated on five DFAs from the Libxc library against seven exact conditions from Pederson and Burke, using constraint solving to verify or refute condition satisfaction.
key_novelty: First formal verification approach to automatically check whether density functional approximation implementations satisfy known exact conditions.
contributions: XCVerifier tool enabling formal verification of DFA implementations
Evaluation on five Libxc DFAs demonstrating feasibility of the approach
Identification of violations and verification results for seven exact conditions
Evidence that formal methods can scale to real scientific software

metrics.other: verification success/failure rate on DFA-condition pairs

limitations: XCVerifier times out on all SCAN functional conditions, indicating scalability challenges with more complex approximations.
